transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Patel (Redwood SE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Marta Lopez (Acme Health, CTO); Ben Carter (ML Eng); Ravi Shah (SRE); Tina Nguyen (Product)
Shared links: Benchmark spreadsheet - https://redwood.app/bench/acme-poc ; Runbook draft - https://redwood.app/runbooks/acme ; Security pack (sent earlier)

Summary:
Quick sync to review this week's benchmark results comparing Redwood POC runs to the customer's baseline provider, discuss tuning knobs (batching, quantization, KV cache), and agree next steps for a dedicated capacity tail-latency run. Some transcription errors expected (KV cash / pairing).

Topics:
- Latency comparison (p50, p95, tail)
- Throughput and batching behavior
- Memory/KV cache hit rates and warmup behavior
- Cost vs latency tradeoffs, dedicated vs hosted
- Next steps and benchmarks to run on dedicated pool

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan Kim: okay hey everyone thank you for joining. uh quick roll call, then we'll jump into the numbers - we have the sheet up, yes?
00:14 Marta Lopez: yep we can see it, thanks. uh, big question for us this week was tail latency for long context prompts.
00:28 Priya Patel: right so we ran the three workloads you shared — short chat, mid-doc summarize, and long-context extraction — and compared against your baseline provider. overall p50 is comparable, p95 is better on Redwood for mid and short, but tails for long context were slightly worse at our default config.
00:48 Ben Carter: can you quantify "slightly"? like are we talking 10% or 2x?
01:02 Priya Patel: yeah, good point. short: p50 about 20ms faster; p95 about 15% better. long-context p95 similar, but p99 tail was roughly 1.8x worse in our hosted config — that was with default batching and warm start, we didn't have dedicated reserved GPUs.
01:22 Ravi Shah: that matches the traces we sent where some requests hit cold KV and we saw spikes. is that right?
01:34 Priya Patel: yep spikes correlate with KV miss windows and also with larger batch formation at the 64-token boundary, so you get slightly longer multiplexing wait.
01:50 Jordan Kim: to be clear, those numbers were from the shared sandbox pool, not the dedicated pool. on dedicated we expect much tighter tail bounds once we pin resources and tune batching.
02:05 Marta Lopez: okay, so the baseline provider is currently giving us more consistent tails?
02:12 Priya Patel: in this test environment yes for long tails. baseline was pinned to 1:1 GPU per worker so no noisy neighbors; our sandbox had more variable workload. when we ran a small dedicated run last week in a similar model size we saw p99 drop closer to baseline.
02:32 Ben Carter: can you share the dedicated run numbers side-by-side? I wanna see memory utilization too.
02:40 Priya Patel: sure, in the spreadsheet tab 'dedicated-run-06-11' we included p50/p95/p99 plus mem, kv hit %. dedicated p99 for long-context was 380ms vs baseline 340ms, mem peak 46GB vs baseline 50GB. kv hit improved from 62% to 89% after KV warmup and prefix caching.
03:04 Liam O'Connor: there's also the quantization profile we applied — 4-bit int8-ish config reduced memory and improved throughput with small quality delta. we saw about 1.2x throughput on identical HW.
03:20 Tina Nguyen: how did quality look? we have clinical extractors, so precision is important.
03:28 Priya Patel: we ran the eval set you sent, rouge/f1 differences were within noise for summarization, extraction tasks still stayed within your pass thresholds, but we flagged 3 prompts for manual review in the sheet.
03:44 Marta Lopez: okay that's helpful. on cost, baseline's proposal is a fixed VM with moderate cost; what's Redwood's expected unit cost post-optimizations?
03:58 Jordan Kim: depends on routing and pooling. with dedicated reserved pool and quantization, our estimate in the sheet is ~30% lower per-inference unit compared to baseline at your expected QPS. but that's model and config dependent.
04:14 Ravi Shah: what about encryption and audit logs? any impact on perf? we need KMS/HSM integration and full audit trails.
04:26 Jordan Kim: security team confirmed KMS support; negligible perf impact for the encryption-at-rest paths. audit logs are separate and don't sit inline in the token path. we'll send the security pack again.
04:38 Ben Carter: can you run a tail-latency focused run on dedicated hardware next week? we want to reproduce the worst-case from production traces.
04:50 Priya Patel: yes, that's the plan. we'll do a focused test with pinned capacity, pre-warmed KV, and a synthetic burst pattern to mimic your traces. we'll also toggle batching thresholds to measure tradeoffs.
05:06 Marta Lopez: timeline?
05:09 Priya Patel: aiming for early next week, Thu-Fri window, but Jordan will coordinate.
05:16 Jordan Kim: I'll send a calendar invite and a short runbook.
05:20 Ben Carter: also please include the exact seed prompts and the request distribution, we need reproducibility.
05:28 Priya Patel: noted, we'll attach request histograms and the exact payloads.
05:36 Marta Lopez: any concerns about model variants? we saw the baseline using a pruned variant.
05:42 Liam O'Connor: we can do model variant comparisons — we've got a quantized pruned variant and the full fp16 variant. the spreadsheet compares both. pruning helps tails but sometimes hurts extraction fidelity.
06:00 Tina Nguyen: will that affect our QA signoff?
06:04 Priya Patel: we'll include evals for the pruned variant too; if extraction drops below your threshold we won't recommend it.
06:12 Ben Carter: on the sandbox runs I noticed some mis-attrs in logs, e.g., KV cash spelled wrong in a few lines, so watch for that when you parse.
06:22 Jordan Kim: chuckle, yeah auto-transcription and some log parsers are messy.
06:26 Marta Lopez: competitors — we briefly looked at Anthropic and SageMaker for the reserved model, but they didn't offer the same prefix caching or observability.
06:38 Jordan Kim: right our caching + trace-level observability is a differentiator.
06:42 Ravi Shah: are there any limits for burst capacity? during end-of-day we see 3x normal QPS.
06:50 Priya Patel: with dedicated reserved capacity you can configure burst pools and auto-burst to a flexible pool; we'll show config options in the runbook. there is a brief warm-up effect for KV and batch formation, but burst config mitigates it.
07:08 Ben Carter: please make sure the run includes tail-latency 1000+ concurrent synthetic requests; production saw some 95th spikes under that pattern.
07:20 Priya Patel: yes, we'll replicate the exact concurrency and the percentiles you care about (p50,p95,p99,p999 if you want).
07:28 Marta Lopez: last thing, pricing — after the dedicated run can you give a committed reserved quote for 6 months?
07:35 Jordan Kim: yes, we'll produce a quote; I just need the expected commit level (we put a draft in the sheet).
07:44 Tina Nguyen: ok thanks.
07:46 Jordan Kim: recap quick: Jordan share benchmark spreadsheet and runbook (action), Priya schedule dedicated tail run, Ben share traces + success criteria. we'll target mid-next-week for results and decision.
07:59 Marta Lopez: sounds good, thanks all.
08:02 Jordan Kim: thanks, bye.

Post-call notes:
- Benchmarks: Redwood shows strong p95 improvements on short/mid workloads; tail p99 for long context needs dedicated pinned run to match baseline.
- Tuning: Enable prefix caching, adjust batching threshold, try quantized pruned variant if extraction quality holds.
- Risks: Sandbox noisy neighbors affecting tails; need dedicated runs for final comparison.
- Next meeting: follow-up after dedicated tail run (TBD), likely next week.
